newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Two die and more 150 ill in Manila cholera outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Two die and more 150 ill in Manila cholera outbreak.

text.p: A cholera outbreak has killed two people in Manila and 150 people, mostly children, have come down with the disease, Philippine health officials said on Saturday.

The Department of Health said a four-year-old girl and a boy of the same age died earlier this week, and that 150 people had been treated in hospital from September 1 to 6 for accute diarrhoea and abdominal pains. Stool tests carried out on a selection of the patients tested positive for the cholera organism.
"The number of culture-positive stool samples would already confirm our diagnosis -- that there is an outbreak of cholera now," Health secretary Carmencita Reodica told reporters.
The cholera outbreak was due to the contamination of drinking water in flood-prone areas in the city, doctors in government hospitals said.

But tests on water samples collected by a team of bacteriologists from the Department of Health and the state agency Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) in affected areas in the city tested negative for contamination, MWSS officials said.
Nevertheless, health workers advised residents to boil their water.
Government and health officials also said they have asked the sewerage authority to replace broken and leaking pipes and increase water pressure in affected areas to stop the epidemic.
"The MWSS team assured us that they are working 24 hours to repair leaks," said Department of Health epidemiology chief Manuel Dayrit.
